rag.description: Run multi-batch SQL Server scripts from an automation run, split on GO and GO n lines like sqlcmd. Scripts come from a .sql file or inline text, an optional transaction rolls back every batch on failure, and batch and row totals stay available to later steps for checks.

qa.question: What does the InvokeSqlServerScript plugin do?
qa.answer: It runs a SQL Server script split into batches on GO separator lines and reports the batch count and changed rows.

qa.question: Which parameters does InvokeSqlServerScript support?
qa.answer: CommandText or CommandFile supplies the script, the Base64 switch decodes a Base64-encoded CommandText, and CommandTimeout, Transaction, and NoEntity tune the run. Credentials, ConnectionString, or discrete values such as Server and Database select the connection.

qa.question: How does InvokeSqlServerScript integrate with G4 workflows?
qa.answer: It is an Action task that uses ActionRuleModel and writes InvokeSqlServerScript:BatchCount and InvokeSqlServerScript:RowsAffected as Base64-encoded session parameters.

qa.question: What are best practices for InvokeSqlServerScript?
qa.answer: Use CommandFile for long scripts, use CommandFile or a Base64-encoded CommandText with the Base64 switch for SQL that contains ` --` or `}}`, and add Transaction so a failing batch leaves no partial changes.

qa.question: How does InvokeSqlServerScript run an inline script that contains ` --` or `}}`?
qa.answer: Encode the whole script, GO lines included, as UTF-8 Base64, pass it as CommandText, and add the Base64 switch. The script is decoded first and then split into batches, while CommandFile content is always read as plain text.

qa.question: How is an InvokeSqlServerScript rule and script written?
qa.answer: Use $type Action, pluginName InvokeSqlServerScript, and an argument such as {{$ --CommandFile:C:\Scripts\deploy.sql --Credentials:sql-production --Transaction}}. Inside the script, a line that holds only GO ends a batch, GO n runs the preceding batch n times, and splitting is line based like sqlcmd.

qa.question: What metadata identifies the InvokeSqlServerScript manifest?
qa.answer: The key is InvokeSqlServerScript, the version is 4, the plugin type is Action, the namespace is G4.Plugins.SqlServer, the category is SqlServer, and the author is Roei Sabag.

qa.question: What behavior does the InvokeSqlServerScript manifest describe?
qa.answer: It describes running multi-batch deployment, migration, and seeding scripts in order and reporting batch and row totals to later steps. Documentation: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/docs/Actions/InvokeSqlServerScript.md Source: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/src/G4.Plugins.SqlServer/Actions/InvokeSqlServerScript.cs

qa.question: What errors can stop InvokeSqlServerScript?
qa.answer: The step fails when neither CommandText nor CommandFile is set, the file is missing, CommandText is not valid Base64 while the Base64 switch is set, no server is resolved, or a batch fails. Batches after the failing one do not run, and Transaction rolls back the earlier ones.

description: ### Purpose
Runs a multi-batch SQL Server script, split on GO separator lines the same way sqlcmd splits it.
Runs deployment, migration, and seeding scripts from a .sql file or inline text, optionally inside one transaction.
Reports how many batches ran and how many rows changed so later steps can confirm the result.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature              | Description                                                                                          |
| Batch splitting      | Splits the script on lines that hold only `GO` or `GO n`, in any letter case.                        |
| Batch repetition     | Runs the preceding batch `n` times for a `GO n` separator.                                            |
| Script sources       | Reads the script from `CommandText`, Base64 `CommandText` with `Base64`, or the UTF-8 `CommandFile`. |
| Ordered execution    | Runs batches in script order on one connection and stops at the first failing batch.                  |
| Optional transaction | Commits after the last batch or rolls back every batch on failure when `Transaction` is present.      |
| Per-batch timeout    | Applies `CommandTimeout` to each batch separately.                                                   |
| Run totals           | Returns `BatchCount` and the summed `RowsAffected`.                                                  |
| Flexible connection  | Connects through a credentials record, a connection string, discrete values, or a Microsoft Entra token. |
| Entity control       | Omits the response entity when `NoEntity` is present while still writing session parameters.         |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case                  | Description                                                                         |
| Deploy database changes   | Apply versioned schema scripts with `GO` separators as one transactional step.       |
| Load reference data       | Run seeding scripts that insert lookup values before a business process starts.     |
| Run maintenance scripts   | Execute cleanup or index maintenance scripts on a schedule.                          |
| Reuse existing SSMS files | Run scripts written for SQL Server Management Studio or sqlcmd without editing them. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case                | Description                                                                        |
| Build a test database   | Create tables, views, and seed rows before a test suite runs.                      |
| Reset test data         | Truncate and reload tables between test runs to keep results repeatable.           |
| Generate load data      | Repeat an insert batch with `GO n` to create many rows for volume tests.           |
| Verify migration safety | Run a migration with `Transaction` and confirm that a failure leaves no changes.   |
### Batch Splitting
- A separator is a line that holds only `GO`, optionally followed by a repeat count, such as `GO 3`.
- `GO` is not case sensitive and may have surrounding spaces, but a separator line cannot hold other text or a comment.
- `GO n` runs the preceding batch `n` times, and each repetition counts toward `BatchCount`.
- Splitting is line based like sqlcmd, so a `GO` line inside a block comment or a multi-line string is still a separator.
- Batches that hold only white space are skipped, and sqlcmd commands such as `:setvar` or `:r` are not supported.
- With the `Base64` switch, `CommandText` is decoded from UTF-8 Base64 first and then split the same way.
### Connection Resolution
1. `Credentials` selects a stored SQL Server credentials record by name or id.
2. When no record matches, a `Credentials` value that contains `=` is used as a raw connection string, and any other value is used as a raw Microsoft Entra access token.
3. Without `Credentials`, `ConnectionString` supplies the baseline connection.
4. `Server`, `Port`, `Database`, `Authentication`, `Username`, `Password`, `Encrypt`, `TrustServerCertificate`, and `Token` override the baseline values they set.
5. The step fails when no server is resolved.
Session parameters are named `InvokeSqlServerScript:<Name>` and are Base64-encoded, so decode them before use.
Holds the number of batches the script ran, as plain integer text.
Counts each repetition of a GO n separator as a separate batch, and empty batches are not counted.
Returned in plain text in the response entity unless NoEntity is set.
entity.name: BatchCount

description: Holds the total number of rows changed by INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE statements across all batches, as plain integer text.
Batches that report no row count, such as DDL statements or batches under SET NOCOUNT ON, add 0 to the total.
Returned in plain text in the response entity unless NoEntity is set.
entity.name: RowsAffected

edge_cases: A failing batch rolls back every earlier batch
CommandFile points to a missing file
Script contains a statement that cannot run inside a transaction
annotations.expected_result: Every batch of deploy.sql runs in one committed transaction, and the batch count and changed rows are stored in InvokeSqlServerScript:BatchCount and InvokeSqlServerScript:RowsAffected.
annotations.notes: deploy.sql holds a CREATE TABLE batch, a CREATE VIEW batch, and an INSERT batch separated by GO lines, so BatchCount is 3. The stored record sql-production supplies the server localhost,1433 and the login. CommandTimeout of 120 seconds applies to each batch separately.

description: ### Deploy a script file in one transaction
Runs C:\Scripts\deploy.sql through the stored credentials record sql-production, batch by batch in script order.
Transaction commits after the last batch succeeds and rolls back every batch when one fails.

edge_cases: GO line with trailing text is not a separator
Plain inline SQL with a space followed by two dashes ends the argument value early unless it is Base64-encoded
SET NOCOUNT ON makes RowsAffected report 0
annotations.expected_result: The table batch runs once and the insert batch runs five times, so InvokeSqlServerScript:BatchCount is 6 and InvokeSqlServerScript:RowsAffected is 5, and the response has no entity.
annotations.notes: The Credentials value contains equals signs and matches no stored record, so it is used as a raw connection string. The inline script uses line breaks, a GO line, and a final GO 5 line. NoEntity keeps the results only in session parameters.

description: ### Repeat an inline batch with a raw connection string
Creates dbo.LoadProbe when missing, then repeats a single-row insert five times with a `GO 5` separator.
The Credentials value is a raw connection string to localhost,1433, and NoEntity omits the response entity.

edge_cases: Base64 switch is absent, so the encoded text is sent as SQL and the step fails
CommandText is not valid Base64, so the step fails before connecting
GO line that also holds a comment is not a separator, so comments stay on statement lines
annotations.expected_result: Both batches run in one committed transaction, so InvokeSqlServerScript:BatchCount is 2 and InvokeSqlServerScript:RowsAffected is 1.
annotations.notes: The Base64 switch decodes CommandText from UTF-8 Base64 before the script is split, so the ` --` comments and line breaks travel inline without ending the argument value. The decoded script holds two batches separated by GO lines, and Transaction rolls both back when either one fails.

description: ### Run a Base64-encoded two-batch script with comments
The argument binds the stored credentials record sql-production, a Base64 CommandText, and the Base64 and Transaction switches.
The decoded script creates dbo.DeployLog when missing and then inserts one row, with a ` --` comment after each statement and a GO line closing each batch.
Holds the number of batches the script ran, as plain integer text.
Counts each repetition of a GO n separator as a separate batch, and empty batches are not counted.
Helps confirm that the whole script was split and executed as expected.
Stored as a Base64-encoded session parameter, so decode it before use.

Stored as a Base64-encoded session parameter, so decode it before use.

description: Selects the sign-in method used to connect to SQL Server.
Overrides the method from the credentials record or the connection string, so one target can switch between SQL logins, Windows sign-in, and Microsoft Entra sign-in.
Leave it empty to keep the method the baseline connection already defines.
parameters.name: Authentication

description: Signs in with a SQL Server login name and password.
Supply the login through Username and Password or through the credentials record.
values.name: Sql Password

description: Signs in with the Windows account that runs the automation.
No user name or password is sent to the server.
values.name: Integrated

description: Signs in with the Microsoft Entra default credential chain, such as environment settings, a managed identity, or a developer tool sign-in.
Fits services that already carry a Microsoft Entra identity.
values.name: Active Directory Default

description: Signs in with the Microsoft Entra identity of the current domain-joined Windows user.
No password is passed in the step.
values.name: Active Directory Integrated

description: Signs in through an interactive Microsoft Entra prompt.
Fits attended runs where a person can complete multi-factor sign-in.
values.name: Active Directory Interactive

description: Signs in with the managed identity of the Azure host that runs the automation.
Username can carry the client id of a user-assigned identity.
values.name: Active Directory Managed Identity

description: Signs in with a Microsoft Entra user name and password.
Accounts that require multi-factor authentication cannot use this method.
values.name: Active Directory Password

description: Signs in as a Microsoft Entra application.
Username carries the application client id and Password carries the client secret.
values.name: Active Directory Service Principal

description: Decodes the CommandText value from UTF-8 Base64 before the script is split into batches.
Encoding the SQL as Base64 lets inline text that contains a space followed by two dashes or a double closing brace travel safely, because those sequences otherwise end an inline argument value.
Only CommandText is decoded, so CommandFile content is always read as plain text.
Invalid Base64 fails the step before anything is sent to SQL Server, so encoded text never runs as SQL.
parameters.name: Base64

description: Points to a UTF-8 .sql file that holds the script, such as C:\Scripts\deploy.sql.
Supports long multi-line scripts, SQL comments, and characters that cannot travel inside an inline argument.
Used only when CommandText is empty, and a missing file fails the step.
parameters.name: CommandFile

description: Provides the script inline, with batches separated by lines that hold only GO or GO followed by a repeat count.
Takes priority over CommandFile, and one of the two is required.

When the SQL contains a space followed by two dashes or two closing braces, use CommandFile or pass the script as UTF-8 Base64 with the Base64 switch, because those characters end an inline argument value.
parameters.name: CommandText

description: Sets how many seconds each batch of the script may run before the step fails with a timeout error.
Defaults to 30 seconds per batch, and the value 0 waits without a time limit.
Missing, negative, or non-numeric values fall back to the 30-second default.
parameters.name: CommandTimeout

description: Supplies a full ADO.NET connection string, such as Server=localhost,1433;Database=Sales;Integrated Security=true.
Used only when Credentials is not set, and discrete values such as Server or Database still override its parts.
parameters.name: ConnectionString

description: Names a stored SQL Server credentials record by its name or id, such as sql-production.
Keeps server addresses, logins, and secrets out of the flow because the record supplies the connection at runtime.
When no record matches, a value that contains an equals sign is used as a raw connection string and any other value is used as a raw Microsoft Entra access token.
Takes priority over ConnectionString when both are set.
parameters.name: Credentials

description: Sets the database the connection opens, overriding the database from the credentials record or the connection string.
Lets one stored login reach several databases on the same server.
parameters.name: Database

description: Sets how the connection encrypts traffic between the automation and SQL Server.
Overrides the encryption mode from the credentials record or the connection string.
parameters.name: Encrypt

description: Requires an encrypted connection and validates the server certificate unless TrustServerCertificate is set.
Matches the default of the Microsoft SQL Server data provider.
values.name: Mandatory

description: Encrypts traffic only when the server asks for it.
Suits older or internal servers that do not offer encryption.
values.name: Optional

description: Uses TDS 8.0 strict encryption, where the secure handshake happens before any login data is sent.
Requires SQL Server 2022 or Azure SQL and always validates the server certificate.
values.name: Strict

description: Omits the response entity so the step returns its results only as session parameters.
Keeps the response small when results are large and only later steps read them.
Session parameters such as InvokeSqlServerScript:BatchCount are still written.
parameters.name: NoEntity

description: Sets the password for the SQL Server or Microsoft Entra login, overriding the password from the credentials record or the connection string.
Prefer Credentials over an inline password so secrets stay out of the flow definition.
parameters.name: Password

description: Sets the TCP port added to Server, such as 1433 for a default SQL Server instance.
Applies only when Server is set in the same step, and values of 0 or less are ignored.
parameters.name: Port

description: Sets the SQL Server host name, address, or named instance, such as localhost or db01\SQLEXPRESS.
Overrides the server from the credentials record or the connection string and is required when neither supplies one.
Combine it with Port to reach a specific TCP port.
parameters.name: Server

description: Supplies a raw Microsoft Entra access token that authenticates the connection.
Fits pipelines that already hold a token for the database resource, and needs Server or a connection string because a token carries no server address.
Do not combine it with Password or an Authentication value, because the data provider rejects a connection that sets both.
parameters.name: Token

description: Runs every batch of the script inside one transaction that commits after the last batch succeeds.
Rolls back all earlier batches when any batch fails, so the database never keeps a half-applied script.
Statements that SQL Server does not allow inside a transaction, such as CREATE DATABASE, fail when the switch is present.
parameters.name: Transaction

description: Accepts the server certificate without checking it against a trusted certificate authority.
Needed for local or test servers that use a self-signed certificate, such as a developer instance on localhost,1433.
Avoid it on production servers because it removes protection against impersonated servers.
parameters.name: TrustServerCertificate

description: Sets the login name used with Password, overriding the user from the credentials record or the connection string.
For a Microsoft Entra service principal, the value carries the application client id.
parameters.name: Username

summary: Runs multi-batch SQL Server scripts from a .sql file or inline text, split on GO and GO n lines like sqlcmd.
Applies deployments, migrations, and seed data in order, with an optional transaction that rolls back every batch on failure.
Reports the batch count and changed rows as session parameters so later steps can verify the run.
